finding.summary: Unrequested semantic change to ALL bounded-range aggregations: `Arguments.iterate` now silently skips blank cells for every range reference, not just unbounded ones
finding.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts: `const isRange = isSrng(node.v); for (const ref of toSrefs([node.v])) { if (isRange) { const cell = grid.get(ref); if (!cell || cell.v === undefined || cell.v === '') continue; } ... }`. The issue only asks for whole-column/row/open-ended lexing + evaluation; this changes the meaning of existing formulas such as `=AVERAGE(A1:A10)` or `=COUNT`/`=MIN`/`=MAX` over a partially-empty bounded range. Worse, the design doc presents it as pre-existing behavior — docs/design/sheets/formula.md: "Blank cells inside a range contribute nothing to aggregations (`Arguments.iterate` skips them)" — so the doc does not record that a cross-cutting evaluation-semantics change was made here. If blank-skipping is genuinely required for `AVERAGE(B2:B)` = 200, that should be stated as an intentional, documented semantics change with its own note in the design doc.
